core_obligations: The forward direction: the Tits algebra of the natural representation being the quaternion algebra itself forces the algebra not to split over the real numbers, by the author's equivalence (proof lines 740-743).

The parity split: the proof then separates the even and the odd case; in the even case the remaining Tits algebras are quaternion algebras, so their base change to the real numbers can be compared directly, and in the odd case the relevant invariant is the even Clifford algebra of the Hermitian form (proof lines 743-762).

The reduced-norm condition: in the even case the criterion becomes the condition that the reduced norm of the Hermitian matrix, computed in the full matrix algebra over the division algebra, be a square in the rational numbers (proof lines 743-762).
The converse: the proof closes by verifying that under either of the two alternatives every Tits algebra satisfies the base-change condition of the author's equivalence (proof lines 762-765).
proof_roadmap: 正向：自然表示的 Tits 代数是四元数除法代数本身，由 RunivIff 得 D 在 R 上不分裂。
再按 k 的奇偶分：k 偶时其余 Tits 代数是四元数代数，判据化为 B 的约化范数是 Q 中的平方；k 奇时判据是偶 Clifford 代数 C^0_D(B,τ_r) 分裂。最后反向验证两种情形都满足基变换条件。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the R-universality criterion for a unitary algebra over a quaternion division algebra with the reversion involution (author lem at source lines 720-735, label SO(quat)), with the criterion split according to the parity of the size into a reduced-norm square condition and a splitting condition for the even Clifford algebra. The proof (source lines 737-765) identifies the Tits algebra of the natural representation with the division algebra (proof lines 740-743), then treats the two parities separately: in the even case the remaining classes are quaternion algebras and can be compared after base change, while in the odd case the even Clifford algebra governs the answer (proof lines 743-764). The parity split is what makes the two alternatives. H2.
